title: How to Get a Voter's Certification
description: Obtain your official Voter's Certification, a valid primary ID and proof of registration while Voter ID cards are discontinued.

requirements.title: Valid ID
requirements.description: A government-issued ID and one photocopy.

requirements.title: Proof of Status
requirements.description: Active voter status confirmed in the COMELEC database.

checklist.title: Verify Status
checklist.description: Confirm that you are an active registered voter who has not been deactivated.

checklist.title: Visit COMELEC
checklist.description: Proceed to the Office of the Election Officer in the city or municipality where you are registered.

checklist.title: Present ID
checklist.description: Provide a valid government-issued ID and a clear photocopy for verification.

checklist.title: Pay Fee
checklist.description: Settle the certification fee at the local treasurer's office and obtain an official receipt.

checklist.title: Receive Certificate
checklist.description: Claim your watermarked Voter's Certification with the official dry seal.

blocks.content: The **Voter's Certification** is an official document issued by the Commission on Elections (COMELEC). Since the physical Voter ID card has been discontinued, this certification serves as its legal substitute.

The Voter's Certification is commonly used for:
*   Primary identification for Passport applications (DFA)
*   Opening bank accounts
*   Proof of active voter status and residency
*   Applying for other government IDs

You may need a Voter's Certification if you are:
- A registered voter who needs a valid Primary ID
- An individual needing proof of residency for local permits
- A traveler needing an alternative document for the DFA

content.title: Benefits of Having a Voter's Certification

blocks.content: While it is a paper document, its high security (watermark and dry seal) makes it a powerful identification tool.

blocks.title: Instant Availability
blocks.content: Unlike the old Voter ID which took years to print, the Certification is issued **Same-Day** at your local COMELEC office.

blocks.title: Legally Recognized
blocks.content: It is officially mandated to be accepted as a **Primary ID** by government agencies and private banks in the Philippines.

blocks.title: Walk-In (Local OEO)
blocks.content: Visit the **Office of the Election Officer (OEO)** in the city or municipality where you are registered.

blocks.title: COMELEC Main Office (Intramuros)
blocks.content: For "National Certification" if you are currently in Metro Manila but registered in a province.
**Pro Tip:** Most ID applications now require **Online Pre-registration**. Always take a screenshot of your QR code or transaction slip before heading to the office.

blocks.title: Visit your Local COMELEC Office
blocks.content: Go to the OEO located at your Municipal or City Hall.

blocks.title: Status Verification
blocks.content: The staff will check the database to confirm you are an **Active Voter**.

blocks.title: Payment
blocks.content: Pay the ₱75 fee at the local Treasurer's Office (usually in the same building). Get the Official Receipt.

blocks.title: Issuance
blocks.content: Present your receipt and ID photocopy back to the OEO. They will print your certification on secure paper and affix the **Official Dry Seal**.

blocks.title: Claim the Document
blocks.content: Your certification is usually ready in 15–30 minutes.

Applicants may process their certification at:
- **Local Office of the Election Officer (OEO):** Found in every City/Municipal Hall.
- **COMELEC Main Office:** Intramuros, Manila (For national central file requests).

Typical processing timelines include:
*   Walk-in: 30 Minutes to 1 Hour (Same Day)
There is no online tracking for certifications as they are issued immediately. You can check your voter status beforehand via the **COMELEC Precinct Finder** (if available online).

Applicants may experience:
- **Deactivated Status:** This happens if you miss two consecutive regular elections. You cannot get a certificate until you reactivate.
- **Records Not Found:** If you recently transferred registration, the records might not yet be in the system.

items: **Wrong Office:** Going to the COMELEC office of where you live now, instead of where you are actually registered.
**Expired ID:** Ensure the ID you present is still valid.

blocks.content: Always check if the certification has the **Raised Dry Seal** before leaving; without it, the document may be rejected by banks or the DFA.

items: Go on a weekday afternoon (2 PM to 4 PM) when there are usually fewer registration applicants.
If you are a Senior or PWD, mention it immediately to be prioritized and have the fee waived.
Bring your own black pen for signing the logbooks.

blocks.title: Can I get a physical Voter ID card?
blocks.content: No. COMELEC has stopped printing plastic IDs to transition to the National ID system. The Certification is the only official document they issue now.

blocks.title: Does the certification expire?
blocks.content: Technically, it proves your status at the time of issuance. Some agencies (like the DFA) may require it to be issued within the last **six (6) months**.
